Points against: the curve shows bundle_share 1.0, buyers 1.0, and top3_share 1.0, which reads as coordinated early buying, not organic demand. The first two minutes after graduation had a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.60, and a launch bot was present. Pool depth is 140 SOL, so a $20 ticket is small relative to liquidity, but round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% plus a 30-second execution lag eat into any edge.

Points for: the classifier labels it ORGANIC, the top-5 buyer share is 39.7%, and the price is only 2.9% off its 30-minute high.

If the desk buys anyway: $5 ticket, 25% stop, 30-60 minute hold, and exit early on any sell wave.

Refuse entirely if the sell pressure in the last 15 minutes (sell volume ~60% of buys) rises further, if the price breaks its 30-minute high and loses the 25% stop level quickly, or if the bundle/top-3 concentration signal is confirmed as operator-backed or a dump setup.

memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution into the recent run-up. The curve data is a red flag: bundle_share and top3_share are both 1.0, meaning one coordinated group, not organic buyers, supplied the early supply, and completer_share of 2.87 suggests that group is the bonding-curve completer many times over. A launch bot was present, and in the first two minutes after graduation 97.7 SOL came in while the sell-to-buy ratio was 0.60, so sellers were already active early. The last 15 minutes show 26 SOL sold against 43.5 SOL bought, with net flow of only 17.5 SOL, so momentum is thinning. The 0.3% drawdown from the 30-minute high is too shallow to read as strength; the +29% return came from bundled volume that can exit on the next leg. With a 140 SOL pool, a $20 ticket faces roughly 1.4-5% round-trip cost, so a modest pullback erases the edge. Skip.
